report.summary: Read the server, Durable Object, egress, daemon, migration, protocol and Mac parts of the change against the Artifacts binding types in apps/tempo/worker-runtime.d.ts and the spec tabs 09 and 10. Ownership checks, credential handling, idempotent merges with lost-acknowledgement recovery, read-only CI egress, CI job token checks and migration preservation all hold. I found no blocking defect. Four non-blocking items: the CI log rewrite may exceed the storage value limit, the merge gate runs before lost-ack recovery when the pushed SHA was not recorded, the Browser Run egress rule is reachable in CI mode (harmless 404), and the Mac view looks read-only before the code view loads. The build, lint and tests were not run (read-only review), and the web UI components were only searched, not read line by line.

findings.text: On every script.output event the CI runner rewrites the whole log tail (up to 1 MiB of UTF-8, from keepTail) into the Durable Object's sync KV. A mostly-ASCII log with any non-Latin-1 character (for example a ✓ or a progress bar) is serialized as UTF-16, about 2 MiB, which may exceed the per-value storage limit. A failed setKv makes event application throw; TempodClient then closes the socket with 1011 and the replay hits the same event, so the job ends as timed_out instead of reporting. The limit is not documented in the repository, so this is not blocking. To confirm, run a workerd test that emits 1 MiB of output containing one '✓'. Separately, rewriting up to 1 MiB on every output event is heavy write amplification.

evidence.why: The value stored on each event can reach about 2 MiB once serialized as UTF-16, and a failed write is replayed after reconnect.

findings.text: Spec 10 says a merge already pushed (lost acknowledgement) is recovered without the gate. When pushedMergeSha was not recorded (the daemon pushed but its response was lost and the one-attempt step failed), the retry checks mergeBlock(headSha) before the daemon's git.merge can find the pushed commit. If a manual rerun of the head SHA is queued, or the pipeline revision changed meanwhile, the retry fails with PR_NOT_MERGEABLE even though the merge is already on the base branch. This is an edge case.

evidence.quote:
const blocked = await core.env.REPOSITORY_CI.getByName(project.id).mergeBlock(merge.headSha);

        if (blocked) throw new TempoError("PR_NOT_MERGEABLE", undefined, blocked);
evidence.why: The gate runs before the daemon's completedMerge recovery path, which differs from the spec's lost-acknowledgement rule.

findings.text: Spec 10 Egress says rules 11–14 never apply in CI mode, but rule 11 (Browser Run) is checked before the CI branch. It is harmless today: browserConnect returns 404 because a CI runner has no workspace row, so no browser session is acquired.

evidence.why: This line runs before `if (config.ci) return decideForCi(...)`, so CI containers can reach the browser path.

findings.text: read_only() treats a missing detail as read-only. If the user selects a repository and switches to Pull requests before the Code load returns, the generation bump discards that response. The view then shows 'This repository is read-only.' and disables New pull request and New workspace until the user returns to Code.

evidence.why: A cancelled detail load leaves detail as None, which is shown as read-only.

checked.risk: Real contracts: Artifacts binding (info, log, readCommit with one trailing newline removed, createToken, import/create, readFile, readTree), compared with the test fakes; Sandbox 1.0 container calls; tempod protocol additions
Failure paths: swallowed errors, failing closed (CI ingest never fails the caller, credential lookup returns null, errors in issue tools and handlers, profile decode fails closed)

Idempotency and state: merge_pr op with pushedMergeSha recovery, daemon operation refs, completeArtifactMerge, CI job tokens, conditional completeJob, ciStart repeated with the same token, ingestion dedupe, issue number counter, PR number allocation

Security: ownership checks, tokens only added by TempoOutbound, CI read-only token and receive-pack blocked, container start env, issue tool project/author from the workspace, redaction, owner-only links

Build and runtime environment: Dockerfile chmod, image test, deploy bindings (REPOSITORY_CI, ARTIFACTS) in wrangler, the deploy script and test config, DO export, D1 migration preserving cascaded child tables
Tests: no sleeps (waitFor and deadline loops on observable state), per-case fixtures, fakes match the real shapes, test file grouping and the CI timing documentation

Spec: tab 10 (components, runs, egress, logs, API, merge gate) and tab 09 (PRs, merges, agent issue tools); spec and implementation notes updated in the same change; Mac client changed with the web UI
